findings.explanation: Splunkbase 5076 is 'Fix hostnames on UFs'; there is no Splunk-built 'Splunk Add-on for Nutanix'. The Nutanix add-on in the catalogue is 'TA for Nutanix Prism' (TA-nutanix, 3103), with a Prism Central variant at 8349. The wrong name/ID repeats in app, references and detailedImplementation (including the `splunk_ta_nutanix*.log` path).
findings.suggested_fix: Cite TA for Nutanix Prism (3103) or the Prism Central TA (8349), and list the sourcetypes and log file names that add-on actually creates; otherwise describe the custom HEC poller as primary.

findings.explanation: In Prism v2.0 the host CPU/memory PPM counters are normally under `stats` (stats.hypervisor_cpu_usage_ppm), while `usage_stats` holds storage counters; v2 hosts carry `cluster_uuid` rather than a cluster name. The UC's field paths (usage_stats.hypervisor_cpu_usage_ppm, memory_size_bytes on VMs) need checking.
findings.quote: per-host physical and usage metrics from `GET /PrismGateway/services/rest/v2.0/hosts/`
findings.suggested_fix: Check one real v2.0 /hosts and /vms response and document the exact JSON paths (stats.*, memory_mb, host_uuid, cluster_uuid) the search depends on.

findings.explanation: description states alert conditions that are just non-zero data checks; the spl actually pages critical on failed N-1 memory headroom or commit-policy breach, high above 92% CPU/memory, warning above 78/82% or memory commit >1.0.
findings.suggested_fix: State the real severity tiers and the N-1 rule (cluster spare memory must be at least the largest host's memory).

findings.explanation: Prism Element shows CPU and memory usage as percentages; PPM is the raw API unit.
findings.quote: Under Hardware, Hosts, pick one node and read hypervisor memory and CPU PPM
findings.suggested_fix: Say to compare the Prism percentage with vcpu_pct_used / mem_pct_used (PPM / 10,000).

firewalled_field_flags.issue: `coalesce(usage_stats.hypervisor_cpu_usage_ppm, ...)` is not quoted, so eval treats `.` as string concatenation of two non-existent fields instead of reading the dotted field; dotted names must be wrapped in single quotes ('usage_stats.hypervisor_cpu_usage_ppm').

`cluster_name=coalesce(cluster_name, clusterName, name)` on host events falls back to the host's own `name`; the eventstats N-1 rollup then runs per host, where spare memory can never cover the largest host's memory, so n1_mem_ok=0 and every such host is critical. n1_mem_ok also defaults to 0 (critical) whenever any input is null, and a cluster-wide N-1 failure is stamped critical on every host in the cluster.
A vCPU overcommit above the default 4.0 is treated as critical alongside N-1 failure; overcommit is a planning threshold, and paging P1 on it will be noisy.
`vm_count_vs_max = vm_count/(lproc*2)` has no defined meaning, and the comment macro carries tunables/authoring notes.

summary: The capacity and N-1 reasoning is explained well, but it rests on a nonexistent 'Splunk_TA_nutanix' at a wrong Splunkbase ID, and the SPL has field-reference and grouping bugs that would mark most hosts critical.
